# COH003 mixed-abstraction-levels

A unit whose callees sit on abstraction layers further apart than the allowed spread.

## What it does

Fires for a function that calls both a high-level and a low-level helper: the layers of its callees differ by more than `max_level_spread` (default 1) of the `[coh]` table in `grimble.toml`. Operators such as slicing and indexing sit on the primitive layer 0. The layer of a callee comes from one of two sources, tried in this order and never mixed. First the grimble model: a `node` declaring `attr layer = N;` and `owns SEL;` puts every function defined in a file the selector surely matches on layer `N`. Second, when the model declares no layer at all, the module depth: a function defined in a deeper directory is a lower-level helper, and when every file sits at one depth the depth places nothing. A callee the layers cannot place leaves the verdict Unresolved, naming those callees, rather than passing silently; a callee that no walked file defines (a library call such as `console.log`) is external and never leaves a verdict Unresolved; with no layers at all the run reports a single repo-level Unresolved note naming the unplaced project callees, not one per file. A callee name defined in several files is placed only when every definition agrees.

## Why it matters

A function that mixes steps of very different abstraction levels is hard to read: the reader switches between the business intent and the byte-level detail in one body.

## Remedy

Extract the low-level steps into a helper on the matching layer, so the function reads at one level.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```python expect=fire file=top.py
def f(order, raw):
    total = price_order(order)
    head = raw[2:5]
    return total, head
```

```python file=price.py
def price_order(order):
    return order
```

```python file=a/b/helper.py
def helper():
    return 1
```

### Clean case 2

```python expect=clean file=top.py
def f(order, raw):
    total = price_order(order)
    return total
```


```python expect=unresolved file=top.py

```
